Sam: heads-up — bringup of quantized reranker-v2 on the dev bench: MRR looks +1.1% but NDCG @10 dropped ~2.4% on the anchor holdout. Can someone sanity-check dataset/formatting? :thinking: Tara: ugh, that's that classic mixed-format surprise. which dataset exactly? anchor vs gold-sampled? Sam: anchor_holdout_v3 (same as previous runs). numbers from EvalBot attached below. I suspect something changed during candidate preprocessing when we switched to the new tokenizer wrapper. Cheng: can you paste the EvalBot output? also did you compare short vs long query slices? seems like NDCG hit often concentrates in long-doc cohorts. EvalBot: eval-run 1711118999 for reranker-v2-ptq (8bit) - dataset: anchor_holdout_v3 (12k queries) - overall: MRR +1.1%, NDCG@10 -2.4% - slice breakdown: short_queries (qlen<=10): NDCG +0.3%, long_queries (qlen>40): NDCG -6.8% - candidate ordering shift: tail candidates (rank >=15) gained score mass -> reordering observed - p_bootstrap(NDCG drop) = 0.085 (not quite <0.05) Tara: interesting. p ~0.085 suggests marginal but not definitive. long_query slice -6.8% is big though. any change to document truncation / snippet extraction? Sam: i double-checked the bringup diff: we replaced html-stripper v1 -> html-stripper v2 (aggressive), and we now do `.strip()` earlier in preprocess. Could've collapsed sentence boundaries and removed inline punctuation used by the model as signals. Cheng: that matches. If the reranker uses in-doc sentence anchors as weak signals, aggressive HTML removal + early trimming can remove anchor text tokens. Quick check: compare token counts and first-50-token diffs between old vs new preprocess for a sample of failing queries. Tara: can we run a tiny experiment: run eval harness with original preprocessing but with quantized model, and with new preprocessing + float model? isolates quantization vs formatting. Sam: yes. plan: three arms 1) float model + old preprocess (gold baseline) 2) quant model + old preprocess (quant-only) 3) quant model + new preprocess (current failing) I'll kick off 1/2 now. Cheng: also add 4) float + new preprocess to see preprocessing-only effect. keep batches small but stratified by qlen. Sam: good call. sample command I'm using: ```bash ./eval_harness --dataset anchor_holdout_v3 \n --model reranker-v2 --quantize 8bit --preproc version=new \n --slice-by qlen --out /tmp/eval-1711119.json ``` (we'll swap flags for the other arms) EvalBot: queued jobs: - job 1711119001: float+old (eta ~15m) - job 1711119002: quant+old (eta ~18m) - job 1711119003: float+new (eta ~15m) - job 1711119004: quant+new (current baseline, finished earlier) Tara: nice. If preprocessing-only explains most of the NDCG drop, we need to revert the html-stripper change or introduce a conservative mode for long docs. If quant-only, then we consider tuning PTQ params (per-channel vs per-tensor) or try hybrid 4bit for KV cache. Cheng: also watch candidate scoring distribution (not just top metrics). If tail mass increases, maybe quantization noise on high-token embeddings -> score smoothing. We can compute KL between score histograms old vs new. Sam: agree. i added histogram comparison to the harness (script will output KL and earth-mover). EvalBot: job 1711119001 complete: float+old => baseline numbers: MRR 0.347, NDCG@10 0.412 EvalBot: job 1711119002 complete: quant+old => MRR 0.350 (+0.9%), NDCG@10 0.407 (-1.2%) EvalBot: job 1711119003 complete: float+new => MRR 0.345 (-0.6%), NDCG@10 0.393 (-4.6%) Tara: ok that's pretty telling — new preprocess alone causes majority of NDCG drop. quant adds a small NDCG loss but not the main culprit. Cheng: can we diff tokenization for the long_query slice? my bet: new preproc truncates or merges delimiter tokens earlier, removing useful context for long docs. Sam: grabbed sample diffs: for a failing case, old preprocess preserves the snippet header "

Answer

" -> tokens include "Answer"; new preprocess stripped that and collapsed neighboring punctuation so the model sees less explicit cue. Tara: let's revert the aggressive html-stripper for the release branch and add a unit test in preprocessing that asserts retention of textual headers (simple heuristic: keep heading text). Also add a QA gate: compare slice NDCG on small holdout before accepting preprocess changes. Sam: action items: - Sam: revert html-stripper change on release branch and run full smoke (in progress) - Cheng: add token-diff unit and histogram KL monitoring to harness (PR incoming) - Tara: add preprocess-sanity check to onboarding checklist (dont let formatting-only changes land without slice NDCG check) Cheng: ping me when PR is up, i'll run long-query focused bench. Sam: thanks. gonna roll back and then re-run quant bringup. will post updated numbers. :thumbsup:
